decisions.choice: good: the true and worthy shepherd, the model of what a shepherd should be
alternatives: morally good as opposed to wicked
decisions.reason: The word (καλός) is not the usual word for moral goodness. It describes what is fine, worthy and as it should be: the shepherd who is everything a shepherd ought to be, set against the thieves and robbers of 10:1, 8, 10 and the hired man of verse 12. It also carries a note of what is admirable, as in 2:10 (the good wine). Its proof is given at once: he lays down his life for the sheep. The Greek puts the article twice, "the shepherd, the good one", which marks him out as the one true shepherd, not one good shepherd among others.

decisions.choice: I am the good shepherd: Jesus claims the shepherd role that the Scriptures give to God and to his promised king
alternatives: only a picture drawn from daily life
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures God is the shepherd of his people (Psalm 23:1; 80:2; Isaiah 40:11). In Ezekiel 34 God condemns the shepherds of Israel who fed themselves and let the flock be scattered, and promises to seek and rescue his sheep himself (34:11-16) and to set over them one shepherd, his servant David (34:23). After the leaders have thrown out the man born blind (9:34), Jesus presents himself as that shepherd. This is one of the "I am" sayings with a predicate (6:35; 8:12; 10:7, 9; 11:25; 14:6; 15:1); the stressed "I" sets him against all false shepherds.

decisions.choice: lays down his life: gives up his life of his own will, by dying
decisions.reason: To lay down one's life (τίθημι with ψυχή) is a way of speaking that John uses again and again: 10:15, 17-18; 13:37-38; 15:13; 1 John 3:16. It means giving up one's life in death, freely. Verses 17-18 make clear that Jesus means his own death, which he gives of his own accord. A shepherd in Israel might risk his life against wild animals (1 Samuel 17:34-35); this shepherd goes further and dies for the flock. Here ψυχή means life itself, not the soul as one part of a person.

decisions.choice: for: on behalf of, for the good of the sheep
alternatives: in the place of the sheep
decisions.reason: The preposition (ὑπέρ) means "on behalf of": the shepherd dies so that the sheep may live. John uses it of Jesus's death in 6:51 (for the life of the world), 11:50-52 (one man dying for the people) and 15:13. In 11:50 the thought of one dying instead of many is near, but the word itself says that the death is for their benefit.

decisions.choice: the good shepherd (every level)
decisions.reason: "Good" in its older, fuller sense of worthy and true covers what the Greek word means (meaning decision m1), and "the good shepherd" is the name by which this saying is known. The Greek leaves little room for other wording, so this sentence is close to other translations; it is not taken from them. Other words for the adjective each catch only part of its sense.

decisions.choice: his: deity_pronoun setting
alternatives: his, with no setting, as for a figure in a picture
decisions.reason: The second half reads like a general saying about any good shepherd, but Jesus has just said that he is the good shepherd, and the saying describes his own death (verses 15, 17-18). The pronoun therefore refers to him and takes the deity_pronoun setting, unlike the shepherd of 10:2-4, a figure in a picture whom Jesus has not yet named as himself.

decisions.choice: gives up his life
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase for the idiom (meaning decision m3) that keeps the sense of a life given freely.

decisions.choice: pone su vida (L); da su vida (B); entrega su vida (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek verb "lay down" (meaning decision m3), which returns in 10:15, 17 and 18; Balanced and Readable use the everyday idiom for giving one's life of one's own will.

decisions.choice: el buen pastor
decisions.reason: As in English: "buen" covers the sense of worthy and true (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: le bon berger; les brebis (every level)
decisions.reason: "Bon" placed before the noun says, as the Greek word does, that he is a shepherd as a shepherd should be (meaning decision m1); "le vrai berger" would set him only against false ones, and "le beau berger" now speaks of looks. "Le bon berger" is also how this saying is known in French. "Brebis" is the usual French word for sheep in a flock that is tended and led, and it is kept for the whole passage (10:1-30); "moutons" is used where animals are sold (2:14).

decisions.choice: dépose sa vie (L); donne sa vie (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek picture of laying something down (meaning decision m3), which is understood in French though it is not an idiom; Balanced and Readable say "donner sa vie", the French idiom for dying freely for others. "Livrer" was avoided because in John it is the verb of betrayal ("livrer" Jesus to his enemies). The same pair is used in verses 15, 17 and 18.

decisions.choice: maisha (for psychē, here and in verses 15-18)
decisions.reason: ψυχὴν here is the shepherd's own life, given up in death. "Uzima" is kept for the life Jesus gives (verse 10), and "roho" for spirit; "maisha" (one's life) is the plain word for what a person lays down. "Uhai" would also serve.

decisions.choice: "người chăn tốt lành" for the good shepherd, at every level
decisions.reason: kalos here means the true, worthy shepherd, the model of a shepherd; "hiền lành" (gentle) is the familiar wording but narrows the sense, and "mục tử nhân lành" is the Catholic form. A reviewer may prefer the familiar title.

decisions.choice: reflexive "mình" for "his" life, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Vietnamese refers back to the subject with "mình", which has no capital form, so the English span for "his" has no counterpart here.

decisions.choice: "Ta" and "các người" kept from 10:1-10
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself as "Ta" and to his hearers as "các người" through this passage (style guide section 6).

decisions.choice: "선한 목자" at every level
decisions.reason: kalos here is the true, model shepherd. "선한 목자" is the form Korean readers know as the title of this saying; Readable keeps it so that the title is the same at every level.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psyche; "내놓는다" (L, B), "내준다" (R)
decisions.reason: psyche here is a person's own life that can be given up by dying, which Korean calls "목숨"; "생명" stays for zoe (10:10). "내놓다" says the giving is his own act; the familiar "버리다" sounds like abandoning.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span in Korean ("자기 목숨"); Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체) through 10:11-18
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); recorded once for this passage, with the speech level of the discourse.

decisions.choice: o bom pastor (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English: "o bom pastor" is the name by which the saying is known in Portuguese, and "bom" before the noun carries the sense of a shepherd who is all a shepherd should be (meaning decision m1), not only a kind one.

decisions.choice: dá a sua vida (L, B); entrega a sua vida (R)
decisions.reason: "Dar a vida por" is the Portuguese idiom for giving up one's life freely for others (meaning decision m3); "depor" would be a calque. The same verb carries through verses 15, 17 and 18 ("dá-la", "eu a dou"), so the thread stays visible. Readable says "entrega", which stresses that the life is handed over freely.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: "his" is a suffix ("ነፍሱን", "ሕይወቱን")
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: "መልካሙ እረኛ" (the good shepherd); "ነፍሱን ... አሳልፎ ይሰጣል" (L), "ሕይወቱን ... አሳልፎ ይሰጣል" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "መልካም" says both good and noble, the model shepherd. Literal keeps the Greek word "soul" ("ነፍስ"); Balanced and Readable say "life". "አሳልፎ መስጠት" (give up, hand over) is the Amharic for laying down one's life; "ያኖራል" would mean he stores it. Used through 10:11-18.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span; plain "अपना" for the good shepherd
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change; in the narrative Jesus takes the honorific third person at every level. When Jesus speaks of himself in the third person, here as the good shepherd, the title takes plain singular forms, as settled in Matthew. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "अपना प्राण देता है" (L, B); "अपनी जान दे देता है" (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom means to give up one's life of one's own will, by dying (meaning decision m3); Readable uses the everyday "जान". The same wording through 10:11-18.

decisions.choice: "Я — добрый пастух"
decisions.reason: "I am" with a predicate takes the dash (docs/john-terms.md). "Добрый" in its older, fuller sense of worthy and true covers the Greek word (meaning decision m1) and keeps the familiar name of the saying; "пастух" is the same word as in 10:2.

decisions.choice: "свою", with no deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The English "his" takes the setting. Russian uses the reflexive "свою", which the style guide leaves without one.

decisions.choice: "добрий пастух"
decisions.reason: The word means the true and worthy shepherd, the model of one (meaning decision m1); "добрий" carries both good and kind and is the familiar form, while "гарний" leans to looks and "справжній" loses the goodness. Literal keeps the Greek order "пастух добрий".

decisions.choice: "своє життя" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Ukrainian uses the reflexive "свій" for the subject's own, and the reflexive takes no span (docs/ukrainian-style.md section 7), where the English has one on "his". The same in 10:15, 10:17.

decisions.choice: "良い羊飼い"; "命を差し出す" (every level, and in 10:15, 17-18)
decisions.reason: "良い" covers the worthy, true shepherd (m1), and the title is the name by which the saying is known; the grammar leaves little room for other wording. For laying down his life (m3), "差し出す" says that the life is given freely, by his own will, as 10:17-18 explain, and is not the wording of the older versions. Readable puts the stress on "わたし" with "が", as in 10:7.

source.text: ὁ μισθωτὸς καὶ οὐκ ὢν ποιμήν, οὗ οὐκ ἔστιν τὰ πρόβατα ἴδια, θεωρεῖ τὸν λύκον ἐρχόμενον καὶ ἀφίησιν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ φεύγει καὶ ὁ λύκος ἁρπάζει αὐτὰ καὶ σκορπίζει ὅτι μισθωτός ἐστιν καὶ οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν προβάτων.

records.literal_gloss: The hired man and not being shepherd, whose not are the sheep own, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters, \v 13 because a hired man he is and not [it] is a care to him about the sheep.

en.L: The hired man, who is not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters [them], \v 13 because he is a hired man and the sheep are no concern to him.
en.B: A hired man is no shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. So when he sees the wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf seizes them and scatters the flock. \v 13 He flees because he works only for pay, and the sheep mean nothing to him.
en.R: A worker hired for pay is not a shepherd, and the sheep do not belong to him. When he sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and gets away. Then the wolf grabs the sheep and chases them in all directions. \v 13 The man gets away because he is only working for the money. He does not really care about the sheep.

es.L: El asalariado, que no es pastor, de quien no son propias las ovejas, ve venir al lobo y deja las ovejas y huye, y el lobo las arrebata y dispersa, \v 13 porque es asalariado y no le importan las ovejas.
es.B: El asalariado no es pastor, y las ovejas no son suyas. Por eso, cuando ve venir al lobo, deja las ovejas y huye, y el lobo las arrebata y dispersa el rebaño. \v 13 Huye porque trabaja solo por la paga, y las ovejas no le importan.
es.R: Un trabajador al que se le paga no es un pastor, y las ovejas no son suyas. Cuando ve venir un lobo, deja las ovejas y se escapa. Entonces el lobo agarra a las ovejas y las hace correr en todas direcciones. \v 13 El hombre se escapa porque solo trabaja por el dinero. En realidad no le importan las ovejas.

fr.L: Le salarié, qui n’est pas berger et à qui les brebis n’appartiennent pas, voit le loup qui vient, et il laisse les brebis et s’enfuit, et le loup s’en empare et [les] disperse, \v 13 parce qu’il est salarié et que les brebis ne lui importent pas.
fr.B: Le salarié n’est pas un berger, et les brebis ne sont pas à lui. Aussi, quand il voit venir le loup, il abandonne les brebis et s’enfuit, et le loup s’empare d’elles et disperse le troupeau. \v 13 Il s’enfuit parce qu’il ne travaille que pour son salaire et que les brebis ne comptent pas pour lui.
fr.R: Un homme qu’on paie pour garder les brebis n’est pas un berger, et les brebis ne sont pas à lui. Quand il voit arriver un loup, il laisse les brebis et il se sauve. Alors le loup attrape des brebis et fait fuir les autres dans tous les sens. \v 13 L’homme se sauve parce qu’il travaille seulement pour l’argent. Les brebis ne l’intéressent pas vraiment.

sw.L: Kibarua, ambaye si mchungaji, wala kondoo si mali yake, humwona mbwa mwitu akija, naye huwaacha kondoo na kukimbia, na mbwa mwitu huwakamata na kuwatawanya, \v 13 kwa sababu ni kibarua, wala hawajali kondoo.
sw.B: Kibarua si mchungaji, na kondoo si wake. Kwa hiyo anapomwona mbwa mwitu akija, huwaacha kondoo na kukimbia, na mbwa mwitu huwakamata na kulitawanya kundi. \v 13 Hukimbia kwa sababu anafanya kazi kwa ajili ya mshahara tu, wala kondoo si kitu kwake.
sw.R: Mfanyakazi aliyeajiriwa si mchungaji, na kondoo si wake. Anapomwona mbwa mwitu akija, huwaacha kondoo na kukimbia. Kisha mbwa mwitu huwakamata kondoo na kuwafukuza kila upande. \v 13 Mtu yule hukimbia kwa sababu anafanya kazi kwa ajili ya fedha tu. Hawajali kondoo kwa kweli.

vi.L: Người làm thuê, vốn không phải là người chăn, chiên cũng không phải của riêng mình, thấy sói đến thì bỏ chiên mà chạy trốn, và sói cướp lấy chúng và làm [chúng] tan tác, \v 13 vì anh ta là người làm thuê và không lo gì cho chiên.
vi.B: Người làm thuê không phải là người chăn, và chiên không thuộc về anh ta. Vì vậy, khi thấy sói đến, anh ta bỏ chiên mà chạy trốn, và sói vồ lấy chiên, làm cả đàn tan tác. \v 13 Anh ta chạy trốn vì chỉ làm công lấy tiền, và chẳng quan tâm gì đến chiên.
vi.R: Người làm công để lấy tiền không phải là người chăn, và chiên cũng không phải của anh ta. Khi thấy chó sói đến, anh ta bỏ chiên lại mà chạy thoát thân. Rồi sói vồ lấy chiên và đuổi chúng chạy tán loạn. \v 13 Người ấy bỏ chạy vì anh ta chỉ làm việc để lấy tiền. Anh ta không thật sự lo cho chiên.

ko.L: 삯꾼, 곧 목자가 아니고 양들이 자기 것이 아닌 사람은 이리가 오는 것을 보고 양들을 내버려 두고 도망친다. 그러면 이리는 그것들을 낚아채고 흩어 버린다. \v 13 그가 삯꾼이고 양들에 대해 마음을 쓰지 않기 때문이다.
ko.B: 삯을 받고 일하는 사람은 목자가 아니고, 양들도 그의 것이 아니다. 그래서 그는 이리가 오는 것을 보면 양들을 내버려 두고 도망치고, 이리는 양들을 덮쳐 양 떼를 흩어 놓는다. \v 13 그가 도망치는 것은 삯을 받고 일할 뿐, 양들에게는 관심이 없기 때문이다.
ko.R: 돈을 받고 일하는 일꾼은 목자가 아니다. 양들도 그의 것이 아니다. 그래서 늑대가 오는 것을 보면 양들을 두고 도망간다. 그러면 늑대가 양들을 덮치고 사방으로 흩어지게 한다. \v 13 그 사람이 도망가는 것은 돈 때문에 일할 뿐이고, 양들을 정말로 아끼지는 않기 때문이다.

pt.L: O assalariado, que não é pastor, de quem as ovelhas não são próprias, vê o lobo vindo, e abandona as ovelhas e foge, e o lobo as arrebata e [as] dispersa, \v 13 porque é assalariado e as ovelhas não lhe importam.
pt.B: O assalariado não é pastor, e as ovelhas não são dele. Por isso, quando vê o lobo chegando, abandona as ovelhas e foge, e o lobo as ataca e espalha o rebanho. \v 13 Ele foge porque trabalha só pelo salário, e as ovelhas não significam nada para ele.
pt.R: Um homem contratado por dinheiro não é pastor, e as ovelhas não pertencem a ele. Quando vê um lobo chegando, ele abandona as ovelhas e foge. Então o lobo agarra as ovelhas e as espalha para todos os lados. \v 13 O homem foge porque só está trabalhando pelo dinheiro. Ele não se importa de verdade com as ovelhas.

hi.L: मज़दूर, जो चरवाहा नहीं है और भेड़ें जिसकी अपनी नहीं हैं, भेड़िये को आते देखता है और भेड़ों को छोड़ देता है और भाग जाता है, और भेड़िया उन्हें पकड़ लेता है और [उन्हें] तितर-बितर कर देता है, \v 13 क्योंकि वह मज़दूर है और उसे भेड़ों की कोई चिंता नहीं।
hi.B: मज़दूरी पर रखा गया आदमी चरवाहा नहीं है, और भेड़ें उसकी अपनी नहीं हैं। इसलिए जब वह भेड़िये को आते देखता है, तो भेड़ों को छोड़कर भाग जाता है, और भेड़िया उन्हें पकड़ लेता है और झुंड को तितर-बितर कर देता है। \v 13 वह इसलिए भागता है कि वह केवल मज़दूरी के लिए काम करता है, और उसे भेड़ों की कोई परवाह नहीं।
hi.R: जो आदमी पैसों के लिए काम पर रखा जाता है, वह चरवाहा नहीं होता, और भेड़ें उसकी अपनी नहीं होतीं। जब वह भेड़िये को आते देखता है, तो भेड़ों को छोड़कर भाग जाता है। फिर भेड़िया भेड़ों को पकड़ लेता है और उन्हें चारों ओर भगा देता है। \v 13 वह आदमी इसलिए भाग जाता है क्योंकि वह बस पैसों के लिए काम करता है। उसे भेड़ों की सचमुच कोई परवाह नहीं।

ru.L: Наёмник же, и не пастух, которому овцы не свои, видит волка приходящего, и оставляет овец, и бежит, и волк хватает их и разгоняет [их], \v 13 потому что он наёмник и нет ему дела до овец.
ru.B: Наёмник — не пастух, и овцы ему не принадлежат. Поэтому, когда он видит, что идёт волк, он бросает овец и убегает, а волк хватает их и разгоняет стадо. \v 13 Он убегает, потому что работает только ради платы и овцы ему безразличны.
ru.R: Работник, которого наняли за плату, — не пастух, и овцы ему не принадлежат. Когда он видит, что идёт волк, он бросает овец и убегает. Тогда волк хватает овец и разгоняет их в разные стороны. \v 13 Этот человек убегает, потому что работает только ради денег. Ему на самом деле нет дела до овец.

uk.L: Найманець, який і не пастух, якому вівці не свої, бачить вовка, що йде, і покидає овець, і втікає, і вовк хапає їх і розганяє, \v 13 бо він найманець, і не дбає він про овець.
uk.B: Найманець — не пастух, і вівці не його власні. Тож коли він бачить, що йде вовк, то покидає овець і втікає, а вовк хапає їх і розганяє отару. \v 13 Він утікає, бо працює лише за плату, і вівці йому байдужі.
uk.R: Чоловік, якого найняли за гроші, — не пастух, і вівці йому не належать. Коли він бачить, що йде вовк, то покидає овець і втікає. Тоді вовк хапає овець і розганяє їх на всі боки. \v 13 Чоловік утікає, бо працює тільки за гроші. Йому насправді байдуже, що буде з вівцями.

ja.L: 雇い人で、羊飼いでなく、羊が自分のものでない者は、狼が来るのを見ると、羊たちを置き去りにして逃げる。そして狼は羊たちを奪い、[群れを]散らす。\v 13 彼は雇い人であって、羊たちのことを心にかけていないからである。
ja.B: 雇い人は羊飼いではなく、羊も自分のものではない。だから、狼が来るのを見ると、羊を置き去りにして逃げる。そして狼は羊を奪い、群れを散らしてしまう。\v 13 彼が逃げるのは、報酬のためだけに働いていて、羊のことなど気にかけていないからである。
ja.R: お金で雇われて働く人は、羊飼いではない。羊もその人のものではない。だから、おおかみが来るのを見ると、羊を置いて逃げてしまう。すると、おおかみは羊に襲いかかり、群れをちりぢりにする。\v 13 その人が逃げるのは、お金のためだけに働いているからだ。羊のことを本当には心配していないのだ。

decisions.choice: the hired man: a worker paid to watch the flock, who has no stake in it
decisions.reason: Flocks were often kept by the owner or his family (Genesis 29:9; 1 Samuel 16:11), but hired men were also used. A man paid by the day stood to lose nothing of his own if the flock was lost. The contrast is drawn twice: he is not a shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. The good shepherd, by contrast, calls the sheep "my own" (verse 14; compare 10:3-4).

decisions.choice: and not being a shepherd: "and" adds a description of the same man
alternatives: the hired man and someone else who is not a shepherd
decisions.reason: Only one person is meant. The little word "and" joins a second description to the first: the hired man, who is also no shepherd. Verse 13 speaks of him alone.

decisions.choice: the wolf that snatches and scatters: the danger the flock faces when its keepers fail
alternatives: a particular enemy Jesus has in mind
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the people of God are scattered and become prey for wild animals when their shepherds care only for themselves (Ezekiel 34:5-8; Zechariah 11:16-17; compare Jeremiah 23:1-2). The wolf is part of the picture; Jesus does not say whom it stands for. Scattering the flock is undone by the shepherd who gathers (verse 16; 11:52).

decisions.choice: the sheep are no concern to him: he does not care what happens to them
decisions.reason: The phrase (μέλει) means "it matters to someone"; with "not" it means that he has no concern for them. It explains why he runs: his care is for his pay, not for the flock. In the setting of chapter 9, the picture stands against leaders who cast out one of the flock (9:34), though Jesus does not name the hired man.

decisions.choice: He flees because (B); The man gets away because (R); works only for pay, working for the money
alternatives: because he is a hired man (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable begin verse 13 as a new sentence, so they repeat the verb it explains, and they spell out what being a hired man means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: seizes them and scatters the flock (B); grabs the sheep and chases them in all directions (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek gives "them" once for both verbs; Balanced and Readable supply an object for the second.

decisions.choice: las arrebata y dispersa (L), no bracket
decisions.reason: One Spanish clitic serves both verbs, so Literal needs no bracketed "[them]".

decisions.choice: Huye porque (B); se escapa porque (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: verse 13 begins a new sentence, so the verb it explains is repeated.

decisions.choice: le salarié (L, B); un homme qu’on paie pour garder les brebis (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a worker paid by the day (meaning decision m1). "Mercenaire" is the traditional word in French Bibles, but today it means a hired soldier and suggests violence, which the Greek does not. "Berger à gages" would call him a shepherd, which the sentence denies. "Salarié" says only that he works for pay; Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: "người làm thuê" with "anh ta" as his pronoun
decisions.reason: "anh ta" is neutral for a man of no special standing; "nó" or "kẻ" would make him a villain, which the picture does not: he is careless, not a thief.

decisions.choice: "삯꾼" (L); "삯을 받고 일하는 사람" (B); "돈을 받고 일하는 일꾼" (R)
decisions.reason: "삯꾼" is the exact Korean word for a hired hand but now sounds old and somewhat contemptuous; Balanced and Readable describe him.

decisions.choice: "이리" (L, B); "늑대" (R)
decisions.reason: Both mean wolf. "이리" is the word long used in Korean Scripture; "늑대" is the common everyday word, used at Readable.

decisions.choice: o assalariado
decisions.reason: "Assalariado" says exactly what the Greek word says, a man who works for wages (meaning decision m1); "mercenário" now suggests a hired soldier, and "empregado" loses the point that he is paid.

decisions.choice: "ቅጥረኛ" (hired man, L, B); "ለደመወዝ የተቀጠረ ሠራተኛ" (a worker hired for pay, R)
decisions.reason: "ቅጥረኛ" names a man who works for wages and so has no stake in the flock, as the meaning decision says; Readable spells this out.

decisions.choice: "雇い人" (L, B), "お金で雇われて働く人" (R); "狼" (L, B), "おおかみ" (R)
decisions.reason: A worker paid to watch the flock, with no stake in it (m1); Readable says what the word means and writes "おおかみ" in kana, as its kanji is outside the Jōyō list.

ja.L: わたしは良い羊飼いである。わたしは自分のもの[である羊たち]を知っており、わたしのもの[である羊たち]はわたしを知っている。\v 15 それは、父がわたしを知っておられ、わたしが父を知っているのと同じである。そしてわたしは、羊たちのために自分の命を差し出す。
ja.B: わたしは良い羊飼いである。わたしは自分の羊を知っており、わたしの羊もわたしを知っている。\v 15 それは、父がわたしを知っておられ、わたしが父を知っているのと同じである。そしてわたしは、羊のために自分の命を差し出す。
ja.R: わたしが良い羊飼いだ。わたしは自分の羊を知っているし、羊もわたしを知っている。\v 15 それは、父がわたしを知っておられ、わたしが父を知っているのと同じだ。そしてわたしは、羊のために自分の命を差し出す。

decisions.choice: know: a personal knowing that belongs to a relationship
decisions.reason: The shepherd knows each sheep, and they know him, as in 10:3-4 where he calls them by name and they know his voice. In the Scriptures to know someone often means to be bound to them in care and loyalty (Exodus 33:12; Jeremiah 1:5; Amos 3:2). Knowing God in this way is eternal life (17:3).

decisions.choice: just as: the knowing between Jesus and his sheep is like the knowing between the Father and the Son, and comes from it
alternatives: a new sentence beginning with verse 15
decisions.reason: The word (καθώς) both compares and grounds, as often in John (15:9-10; 17:18, 21). The bond between the shepherd and the sheep has its pattern and source in the bond between the Father and the Son. The SBLGNT punctuation joins verse 15 to verse 14 as one sentence.

decisions.choice: mine: the sheep who belong to him
decisions.reason: The Greek has a neuter plural, "the mine", to match "sheep". The sheep belong to the shepherd, unlike those of the hired man (verse 12); in 17:6 Jesus says that those the Father gave him were the Father's, and he gave them to Jesus.

decisions.choice: and mine know me (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "and I am known by mine" (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The older manuscripts have the active "mine know me", which matches the pairing in verse 15 (the Father knows me, I know the Father). Many later manuscripts have the passive "I am known by mine". The sense is close either way. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: those [that are] mine (L); those who are mine (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the repeated phrase without naming the sheep, as the Greek does (meaning decision m3). Readable says "my sheep" and then "they".

decisions.choice: It is the same as the way
decisions.reason: Readable makes verse 15 its own sentence and shows the comparison plainly (meaning decision m2). It uses "gives up my life", as in verse 11.

decisions.choice: las mías
decisions.reason: Spanish "las mías" is feminine, agreeing with "ovejas", so Literal and Balanced keep the repeated phrase without naming the sheep and need no brackets (meaning decision m3). Possessives take no setting.

decisions.choice: Es como el Padre me conoce
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the comparison plainly (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: les {{deity_pronoun:miennes|Miennes}}
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the mine" without naming the sheep (meaning decision m3), and French has the same possessive pronoun, feminine plural to agree with "brebis", so Literal and Balanced need no supplied words. The pronoun is Jesus's own, so it takes the deity_pronoun setting as the English "mine" does, with only the capital changing. Readable names "mes brebis".

decisions.choice: "những ai thuộc về Ta" for "the mine"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese says "those who belong to me" with the verb "thuộc về", so no word needs brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: "[그것은] ... 아는 것과 같다"
alternatives: joining 15 to 14 in one Korean clause
decisions.reason: Korean puts the comparison after the clause it compares, so verse 15 needs a subject pointing back to verse 14; it is supplied in brackets to keep each verse's content after its marker.

decisions.choice: "내 양들" (B, R) for "the ones that are mine"
decisions.reason: Korean "내 것들" for people sounds like things; the context is the sheep, so Balanced and Readable say "내 양들".

decisions.choice: as [que são] minhas (L); as que são minhas (B)
decisions.reason: The feminine "as ... minhas" agrees with "ovelhas", as the Greek neuter agrees with "sheep" (meaning decision m3), so Portuguese keeps the phrase without naming the sheep and the reader still knows what is meant.

decisions.choice: "አብ" (the Father); "አባቴ" (my Father)
decisions.reason: "አብ" is the living church word for God the Father and is short enough for every level; with "my" the ordinary "አባቴ" is used, as in Matthew. Used for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: "моих ... мои"
decisions.reason: Russian can use the possessive alone for "those who are mine", as the Greek does (meaning decision m3), so Literal needs no bracket. Readable names the sheep.

decisions.choice: "わたしのもの[である羊たち]" (L); "自分の羊", "わたしの羊" (B, R); "知っておられ" for the Father
alternatives: "わたしのもの" alone at Balanced
decisions.reason: "わたしのもの" alone reads in Japanese as "my things"; Literal brackets the sheep that the neuter plural refers to (m3), and Balanced and Readable name them. Jesus speaks of the Father with the light respect form, as Japanese does for God; this holds through the chapter.

decisions.choice: verse 15 begins a new sentence: "それは……と同じである"
alternatives: "ちょうど……のように" ending the sentence
decisions.reason: The Greek runs verses 14-15 together (m2). Japanese would have to move the comparison before the verb of verse 14, across the verse boundary, so every level starts verse 15 with "それは", which keeps each verse's content after its marker.

source.text: καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης· κἀκεῖνα δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν, καὶ γενήσονται μία ποίμνη, εἷς ποιμήν.

records.literal_gloss: And other sheep I have which not are from the fold this; and-those it is necessary me to bring, and the voice of me they will hear, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.

en.L: And I have other sheep, which are not of this fold; those also I must bring, and they will listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.
en.B: I have other sheep as well, which are not of this fold. I must bring them too, and they will listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, and they will become one flock with one shepherd.
en.R: I have other sheep too. They are not in this sheep pen. I must bring them also. They will listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice. Then they will all be one flock, with one shepherd.

es.L: Y tengo otras ovejas que no son de este redil; también a esas debo traer, y oirán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, y llegarán a ser un solo rebaño, un solo pastor.
es.B: Tengo además otras ovejas que no son de este redil. También a ellas debo traerlas, y escucharán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz, y llegarán a ser un solo rebaño con un solo pastor.
es.R: También tengo otras ovejas. No están en este corral. Tengo que traerlas también. Ellas escucharán {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} voz. Entonces todas serán un solo rebaño, con un solo pastor.

fr.L: Et j’ai d’autres brebis, qui ne sont pas de cet enclos ; celles-là aussi, il {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} faut [les] amener, et elles écouteront {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix, et elles deviendront un seul troupeau, un seul berger.
fr.B: J’ai encore d’autres brebis, qui ne sont pas de cet enclos. Celles-là aussi, je dois les amener ; elles écouteront {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix, et elles formeront un seul troupeau avec un seul berger.
fr.R: J’ai aussi d’autres brebis. Elles ne sont pas dans cet enclos. Je dois les amener, elles aussi. Elles écouteront {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix. Alors elles ne formeront toutes qu’un seul troupeau, avec un seul berger.

sw.L: Na ninao kondoo wengine, ambao si wa zizi hili; hao nao imenipasa kuwaleta, nao wataisikia sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao watakuwa kundi moja, mchungaji mmoja.
sw.B: Nina kondoo wengine pia, ambao si wa zizi hili. Inanipasa kuwaleta hao nao, nao wataisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao watakuwa kundi moja lenye mchungaji mmoja.
sw.R: Nina kondoo wengine pia. Hawamo katika zizi hili. Lazima niwalete nao pia. Wataisikiliza sauti {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Ndipo wote watakuwa kundi moja, lenye mchungaji mmoja.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có những chiên khác, không thuộc chuồng này; những chiên ấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng phải dẫn về, và chúng sẽ nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và chúng sẽ trở thành một đàn, một người chăn.
vi.B: Ta còn có những chiên khác không thuộc chuồng này. Ta cũng phải dẫn chúng về; chúng sẽ nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và sẽ chỉ có một đàn chiên với một người chăn.
vi.R: Ta còn có những chiên khác nữa. Chúng không ở trong chuồng này. Ta cũng phải dẫn chúng về. Chúng sẽ nghe tiếng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Rồi tất cả sẽ thành một đàn, có một người chăn.

ko.L: 그리고 나에게는 이 우리에 속하지 않은 다른 양들이 있다. 그들도 내가 이끌어 와야 한다. 그들은 내 음성을 들을 것이고, 한 양 떼, 한 목자가 될 것이다.
ko.B: 나에게는 이 우리에 속하지 않은 다른 양들도 있다. 나는 그들도 데려와야 한다. 그들도 내 목소리를 들을 것이고, 한 목자 아래 한 양 떼가 될 것이다.
ko.R: 나에게는 다른 양들도 있다. 그 양들은 이 우리 안에 있지 않다. 나는 그 양들도 데려와야 한다. 그들도 내 목소리를 듣고 따를 것이다. 그러면 모두 한 양 떼가 되고, 목자도 한 사람이 될 것이다.

pt.L: E tenho outras ovelhas, que não são deste curral; é necessário que eu traga também essas, e elas ouvirão a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz, e se tornarão um [só] rebanho, um [só] pastor.
pt.B: Tenho também outras ovelhas, que não são deste curral. Preciso trazê-las também, e elas ouvirão a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz, e haverá um só rebanho e um só pastor.
pt.R: Eu tenho outras ovelhas também. Elas não estão neste cercado. Eu preciso trazê-las também. Elas vão escutar a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} voz. Então todas elas vão ser um só rebanho, com um só pastor.

am.L: ከዚህም በረት ያልሆኑ ሌሎች በጎች አሉኝ፤ እነርሱንም ደግሞ ላመጣቸው ይገባኛል፤ ድምፄንም ይሰማሉ፤ አንድ መንጋም ይሆናሉ፤ አንድ እረኛም [ይኖራቸዋል]።
am.B: ከዚህ በረት ያልሆኑ ሌሎች በጎችም አሉኝ። እነርሱንም ደግሞ ማምጣት ይገባኛል፤ ድምፄንም ይሰማሉ፤ አንድ እረኛ ያለው አንድ መንጋም ይሆናሉ።

hi.L: और मेरी और भेड़ें भी हैं, जो इस बाड़े की नहीं; मुझे उन्हें भी लाना अवश्य है, और वे मेरी आवाज़ सुनेंगी, और वे एक झुंड हो जाएँगी, एक चरवाहा [होगा]।
hi.B: मेरी और भी भेड़ें हैं, जो इस भेड़शाला की नहीं हैं। मुझे उन्हें भी लाना है, और वे मेरी आवाज़ सुनेंगी, और वे एक ही चरवाहे का एक ही झुंड बन जाएँगी।
hi.R: मेरी और भी भेड़ें हैं। वे इस बाड़े में नहीं हैं। मुझे उन्हें भी लाना है। वे मेरी आवाज़ सुनेंगी। तब वे सब एक झुंड होंगी, और उनका एक ही चरवाहा होगा।

ru.L: И другие овцы есть у {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}, которые не из этого двора; и тех {{deity_pronoun:мне|Мне}} надлежит привести, и голос {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} они услышат, и станут одно стадо, один пастух.
ru.B: Есть у {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} и другие овцы, которые не из этой овчарни. Их тоже {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} должен привести, и они будут слушать {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} голос, и станут одним стадом с одним пастухом.
ru.R: У {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}} есть и другие овцы. Они не в этом загоне. Их {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} тоже должен привести. Они будут слушать {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} голос. Тогда все они станут одним стадом, и у них будет один пастух.

decisions.choice: other sheep: people outside Israel, the Gentiles, who will come to belong to Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say who they are. In 11:51-52 John explains that Jesus would die not for the nation only but to gather into one the scattered children of God, and in 12:20-32 the coming of Greeks to see Jesus leads him to speak of drawing all people to himself. The Gentiles are the most likely meaning. The words could also mean Jews scattered among the nations (compare 7:35), and the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: fold and flock: two different words, the enclosure and the flock itself
decisions.reason: The first word (αὐλή) is the walled yard where sheep were kept at night, the word used in 10:1. The second (ποίμνη) is the flock, the sheep themselves. Jesus does not say that the other sheep will be brought into this fold, but that the sheep from both places will form one flock. Their unity lies in the one shepherd whose voice they hear, not in one enclosure.

decisions.choice: I must: the necessity of God's purpose
alternatives: a duty he has taken on himself
decisions.reason: The word (δεῖ) is used in John for what God's plan requires (3:14, 30; 4:4; 9:4; 12:34; 20:9). The bringing of the other sheep is part of what the Father has given the Son to do.

decisions.choice: one flock, one shepherd: God's promise of a reunited people under one shepherd
decisions.reason: Ezekiel promises that God will set over his flock "one shepherd, my servant David" (Ezekiel 34:23), and that the divided kingdoms will become one nation with one shepherd over them all (Ezekiel 37:22, 24). Jesus takes up the promise and widens it to take in the other sheep. Compare his prayer that those who believe may be one (17:20-23).

decisions.choice: they will become (SBLGNT, plural)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have the singular verb, so that the sentence reads "there will be one flock". The SBLGNT has the plural, with the sheep as its subject: they will become one flock. The sense is the same. A reviewer should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: fold (L, B); sheep pen (R); flock (every level)
decisions.reason: Two different words are kept apart (meaning decision m2), so that the reader can see that the unity is a flock under one shepherd, not one enclosure. Readable uses "sheep pen", a plainer word for the enclosure.

decisions.choice: listen to
decisions.reason: With this construction the verb means to hear and heed, as the sheep do in 10:3, 27; "listen to" keeps both.

decisions.choice: redil / corral (the fold); rebaño (the flock)
decisions.reason: As in English: two different Greek words are kept apart, so the reader can see that the unity is of the flock, not of one enclosure (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: enclos (every level); troupeau (every level)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words are kept apart (meaning decision m2): the walled yard and the flock itself. "Bergerie" suggests a covered farm building, and it sounds close to "berger", which would blur the contrast with "un seul berger"; "enclos" is the plain word for a walled or fenced yard, and is clear to young readers too, so Readable needs no other word. 10:1 uses the same word at every level.

decisions.choice: "chuồng" for the fold, "đàn" for the flock
decisions.reason: Two different Greek words, the enclosure and the flock itself, kept apart with two Vietnamese words at every level.

decisions.choice: "우리" (fold) and "양 떼" (flock) at every level
decisions.reason: The Greek uses two words, the enclosure and the flock; Korean "우리" and "양 떼" keep them apart, so the point (one flock, not one fold) survives.

decisions.choice: curral (L, B); cercado (R); rebanho (every level)
decisions.reason: As the English, the two Greek words are kept apart (meaning decision m2): "curral" / "cercado" for the enclosure, as in 10:1, and "rebanho" for the flock itself. Portuguese needs "só" to say "one flock, one shepherd" with the stress of the Greek; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: "አንድ እረኛም [ይኖራቸዋል]" (and one shepherd [they will have])
alternatives: "አንድ መንጋ፣ አንድ እረኛም ይሆናሉ" (they will become one flock, one shepherd)

decisions.choice: "बाड़ा" (L, R), "भेड़शाला" (B) for the fold; "झुंड" for the flock
decisions.reason: The Greek has two different words, the enclosure and the flock itself (meaning decision m2); Hindi keeps them apart, so that the unity is a flock under one shepherd, not one enclosure.

decisions.choice: "двор" (L), "овчарня" (B), "загон" (R); "стадо" at every level
alternatives: "одно стадо" at every level for both
decisions.reason: The Greek has two words, the enclosure and the flock (meaning decision m2); Russian keeps them apart, so that the unity is one flock under one shepherd, not one enclosure.

decisions.choice: for this reason ... because: "this" points forward to the clause that follows
decisions.reason: John often uses "for this reason" followed by "because" to state a reason and then spell it out (5:16, 18; 8:47; 12:18, 39). Here the reason is that Jesus lays down his life. What he has said in verses 11-16 is gathered into it.

decisions.choice: the Father loves the Son in his self-giving, which is one with the Father's own will
alternatives: the Son earns the Father's love by dying
decisions.reason: The Father has loved the Son before the world was made (17:24; compare 3:35; 5:20). Jesus's free giving of his life is his perfect obedience to the Father (verse 18; 14:31), and in it the Father's love for him is shown and answered (15:10). The verse does not say that the love began with the death.

decisions.choice: so that I may take it again: his death has its rising in view
alternatives: "with the result that", without a purpose
decisions.reason: The word (ἵνα) states the purpose. Jesus lays down his life not to be lost in death but in order to take it again. The cross and the resurrection are one act of obedience.

decisions.choice: take it again: Jesus will take back his life in the resurrection
alternatives: receive it back from the Father, as a gift only
decisions.reason: The verb (λαμβάνω) can mean "take" or "receive". Jesus speaks of raising up the temple of his body (2:19-21), as here of taking up his life. Elsewhere the New Testament says that God raised him (Acts 2:24; Romans 10:9). The two belong together: verse 18 says that the Father gave him authority to take it again.

decisions.choice: This is why ...: because (B); The Father loves me because (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both halves of the Greek pattern with a colon, so that "this" points forward (meaning decision m1); Readable gives the reason once.

decisions.choice: take it up again (B); take it back again (R)
decisions.reason: "Take it up" and "take it back" make plain that he will have his life again (meaning decision m4). Readable says "give up" for "lay down", as in verse 11.

decisions.choice: Por esto ...: porque
decisions.reason: As in English: keeps both halves of the Greek pattern (meaning decision m1). Spanish "Por esto" needs no bracket.

decisions.choice: recuperarla
decisions.reason: As in English: makes plain that he will have his life again (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: la reprendre (every level)
decisions.reason: French "reprendre" means both to take again and to take back, which is what the Greek says with "again" and "take" (meaning decision m4), so every level can use one ordinary verb, here and in verse 18. Balanced and Readable add "ensuite" to make the order plain: the death first, then the life taken back (m3).

decisions.choice: "bỏ mạng sống mình" (L, B); "hy sinh mạng sống mình" (R)
decisions.reason: "bỏ mạng sống" is the plain modern idiom for laying down one's life of one's own will; R uses "hy sinh" (sacrifice), which new readers know well. The older "phó sự sống" is avoided.

decisions.choice: "다시 얻다" (L, B); "도로 찾다" (R)
decisions.reason: lambano here is taking his life back in the resurrection; Korean "다시 얻다" keeps the plain verb, and Readable "도로 찾다" says "get back" in everyday words without naming the resurrection.

decisions.choice: "полагаю ... принять" (L); "отдаю ... взять" (B); "отдаю ... получить обратно" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the old idiom "полагать жизнь"; Balanced and Readable use "отдавать жизнь", as in 10:11, and say plainly that he will have his life again (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "受ける" (L); "取り戻す" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb can mean take or receive (m4); Literal keeps the open word, and Balanced and Readable make plain that he will have his life again, as in the resurrection.

decisions.choice: takes (SBLGNT, present tense)
alternatives: "took" (some early manuscripts, among them P45 and Codex Vaticanus, and the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus)
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have the past tense: no one took it from me. That reading looks back on the death as a past event. The SBLGNT has the present, which fits the present "I lay it down" in the same sentence. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: of myself: by my own free choice
alternatives: on my own authority, apart from the Father
decisions.reason: Elsewhere Jesus says that he does nothing "of himself", that is, apart from the Father (5:19, 30; 7:28; 8:28, 42). Here the phrase answers "no one takes it from me": he is not forced. The next sentence shows that this free choice is also the Father's command; the two are not in conflict.

decisions.choice: no one takes it: even in his death Jesus is not a victim of others' power
decisions.reason: Others will seek to kill him (5:18; 7:1; 8:59), and he will be put to death, but John shows him in control: no one could seize him before his hour (7:30; 8:20), he tells Pilate that Pilate's power is given from above (19:11), and at the end he hands over his spirit (19:30).

decisions.choice: of my own accord (B); because I choose to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of free choice (meaning decision m2), which "of myself" might hide. Readable names "my life" in place of "it".

decisions.choice: por mi propia voluntad (B); porque yo quiero (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the sense of free choice (meaning decision m2), which "por mí mismo" might hide.

decisions.choice: de moi-même (L); de mon plein gré (B); parce que je le choisis (R)
decisions.reason: French "de moi-même" already means "of my own accord", so Literal keeps the Greek phrase without losing the sense of free choice (meaning decision m2); "par moi-même" would mean "without help". Balanced and Readable say the same thing in everyday words.

decisions.choice: "自分から" (L); "自分の意志で" (B); "自分で決めて" (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means by his own free choice (m2), not apart from the Father; Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

decisions.choice: authority: the right, given to him, and the power to act on it
decisions.reason: The word (ἐξουσία) means a right to act that has been granted, together with the power to carry it out. The Father has given the Son authority to judge (5:27) and authority over all people (17:2). Pilate will claim authority over Jesus's life (19:10), and Jesus will answer that Pilate would have none unless it were given him from above (19:11).

decisions.choice: command: the charge the Father has given the Son
decisions.reason: In John the Father's command to the Son is the whole task he was sent to do and the words he is to speak (12:49-50; 14:31). "This command" covers both laying down his life and taking it again.

decisions.choice: the right ... This is what my Father has commanded me
alternatives: authority ... This command I received (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the authority he has been given (meaning decision m1) and turns the noun "command" into a verb.

decisions.choice: el derecho ... lo que mi Padre me ha mandado
decisions.reason: As in English: an everyday word for the authority he has been given (meaning decision m1). The speech that began at 10:7 closes here.

decisions.choice: autorité (L, B); le droit (R)
decisions.reason: The word means a right granted to someone together with the power to use it (meaning decision m1). "Le pouvoir" says only the second; "autorité" keeps the sense that it was given, which the end of the verse makes explicit. Readable uses "le droit", as the English Readable uses "the right".

decisions.choice: "quyền" for exousia
decisions.reason: "quyền" covers both the right and the power to act on it; "quyền năng" would stress power alone.

exousia is a right given to him together with the power to use it. "권세" is the traditional word; "권한" (authority given) is the plainer modern word; Readable says "권리" (a right), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "계명" (L); "명령" (B)
decisions.reason: entole is the charge the Father gave the Son. "계명" is the word Korean readers know from the commandments; Balanced uses the plain "명령".

decisions.choice: "владу" (L, B), "право" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a right given to him together with the power to use it (meaning decision m1); "влада" holds both, Readable says the plainer "право" as the English Readable says "the right".

decisions.choice: "権威" (L, B), "権利" (R); "命令" (L, B), "命じられた" (R)
decisions.reason: The authority is a right granted with the power to act on it (m1). The command is the Father's charge to the Son (m2). John's ἐντολή is "命令" throughout the book, for the Father's charge and for Jesus' commands to his disciples alike (13:34).

decisions.choice: the Jews: the people who heard Jesus speak, among them some of the Pharisees (9:40)
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Jesus has been speaking to those around him after the healing of the man born blind, among them Pharisees (9:40-41). These hearers are divided: some are hostile, some are open to him (verse 21). So the word does not here mean a united group of authorities hostile to Jesus, and it does not mean the people as a whole: Jesus himself is a Jew (4:9, 22), and so are his disciples.

decisions.choice: division again: the hearers split into opposing sides, as before
decisions.reason: The word (σχίσμα) means a split or rift. John has already told of the crowd divided over Jesus (7:43) and the Pharisees divided over the healing (9:16). "Again" points back to these. Jesus's coming divides those who meet him (compare 9:39).

decisions.choice: these words: what Jesus said in 10:1-18
alternatives: only the last words about his death
decisions.reason: The division is over all he has said about the shepherd and the sheep, ending with his words about laying down his life and taking it again.

decisions.choice: the Jews who were listening (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this scene (meaning decision m1), who are divided, not the authorities as one body. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: were divided (B); did not agree with each other (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb, and Readable names what the words were.

decisions.choice: los judíos que escuchaban
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this scene (meaning decision m1), who are divided, not the authorities, so no "dirigentes".

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level; the imperfect "disaient" (10:20-21) at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (10:11-21), as in 1:19. The passé simple ("se produisit", "furent divisés") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé ("se sont divisés"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. In verses 20-21 every level keeps the imperfect "disaient", because the Greek tense pictures an argument that went on among the hearers (meaning decision m2 of 10:20).

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs qui écoutaient (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the hearers in this scene, some hostile and some open to Jesus (meaning decision m1), not the authorities as one body, so "les chefs juifs" would be wrong. Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people present, so that no reader takes it to mean every Jew.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi at every level in this chapter
decisions.reason: As the English: in this chapter John means the people who heard Jesus (verse 19) and those who gathered round him in the temple (verses 24, 31, 33), not only the authorities. So every level says "Wayahudi", and Balanced and Readable add who they were ("waliokuwa wakisikiliza", "waliokuwa pale").

decisions.choice: "những người Do Thái đang nghe" (B, R), not "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision finds the hearers in general here, among them some Pharisees, so the people's name is kept rather than the leaders'.

decisions.choice: "듣고 있던 유대인들" (B, R), not "유대 지도자들"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision takes "the Jews" here as the people listening to Jesus, not the authorities, so Balanced and Readable keep "유대인들" and say who they were.

decisions.choice: os judeus que estavam ouvindo
decisions.reason: As the English: here the word means the hearers present, who are divided (meaning decision m1), not the authorities as one body, so Balanced and Readable keep "os judeus" and tie it to the people listening.

decisions.choice: "አይሁድ" at every level ("የሚሰሙት አይሁድ", the Jews who were listening, B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "the Jews" here as the people who heard Jesus, not only the authorities, so Balanced and Readable keep the word, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "यहूदी" (L); "सुननेवाले यहूदी" (B, R)

records.literal_gloss: Were saying and many of them, "A demon he has and is raving; why him do you hear?"

en.L: And many of them were saying, "He has a demon and is raving mad; why do you listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: Many of them said, "He has a demon and is out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. Why listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.R: Many of them said, "A demon has driven {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} mad! Why do you listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"

es.L: Y muchos de ellos decían: «Tiene un demonio y está loco; ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}}?».
es.B: Muchos de ellos decían: «Tiene un demonio y ha perdido el juicio. ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}}?».
es.R: Muchos de ellos decían: «¡Un demonio {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ha vuelto loco! ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}}?».

fr.L: Et beaucoup d’entre eux disaient : « Il a un démon et il délire ; pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écoutez-vous ? »
fr.B: Beaucoup d’entre eux disaient : « Il a un démon, il a perdu la raison. Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écouter ? »
fr.R: Beaucoup d’entre eux disaient : « Un démon {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a rendu fou ! Pourquoi est-ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écoutez ? »

sw.L: Na wengi wao walikuwa wakisema, "Ana pepo, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} amerukwa na akili; mbona mnamsikiliza?"
sw.B: Wengi wao walisema, "Ana pepo, na amerukwa na akili. Kwa nini kumsikiliza?"
sw.R: Wengi wao walisema, "Pepo amemrukisha akili! Kwa nini mnamsikiliza?"

vi.L: Nhiều người trong số họ cứ nói: "Ông ta bị quỷ ám và điên rồi; sao các anh nghe ông ta?"
vi.B: Nhiều người trong số họ nói: "Ông ta bị quỷ ám và mất trí rồi. Nghe ông ta làm gì?"
vi.R: Nhiều người trong số họ nói: "Quỷ đã làm ông ta điên rồi! Sao các anh còn nghe ông ta?"

ko.L: 그들 가운데 많은 사람이 말하고 있었다. "그는 귀신이 들렸고 미쳤다. 어찌하여 그의 말을 듣느냐?"
ko.B: 그들 가운데 많은 사람이 말했다. "그는 귀신이 들려서 제정신이 아니다. 왜 그의 말을 듣느냐?"
ko.R: 많은 사람이 말했다. "귀신이 들려서 미친 사람이다! 왜 그 사람 말을 듣느냐?"

pt.L: E muitos deles diziam: "Ele tem demônio e está delirando; por que vocês {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} escutam?"
pt.B: Muitos deles diziam: "Ele tem demônio e está fora de {{deity_pronoun:si|Si}}. Por que escutar o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} diz?"
pt.R: Muitos deles diziam: "Um demônio {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} deixou louco! Por que vocês estão escutando o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} diz?"

am.L: ከእነርሱም ብዙዎቹ እንዲህ ይሉ ነበር፦ «ጋኔን አለበት፤ አብዷልም፤ ለምን ትሰሙታላችሁ?»
am.B: ከእነርሱም ብዙዎቹ እንዲህ አሉ፦ «ጋኔን አለበት፤ አእምሮውንም ስቷል። ለምን ትሰሙታላችሁ?»
am.R: ከእነርሱ ብዙዎቹ እንዲህ አሉ፦ «ጋኔን አሳብዶታል! ለምን ትሰሙታላችሁ?»

hi.L: उनमें से बहुत लोग कहने लगे, "उसमें दुष्टात्मा है और वह पागल है; तुम उसकी क्यों सुनते हो?"
hi.B: उनमें से बहुतों ने कहा, "उसमें दुष्टात्मा है और वह पागल हो गया है। उसकी क्यों सुनते हो?"
hi.R: उनमें से बहुतों ने कहा, "एक दुष्टात्मा ने उसे पागल कर दिया है! तुम उसकी क्यों सुनते हो?"

ru.L: Многие же из них говорили: «Он имеет беса и безумствует; что вы {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} слушаете?»
ru.B: Многие из них говорили: «В {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} бес, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не в своём уме. Зачем {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} слушать?»
ru.R: Многие из них говорили: «Бес свёл {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} с ума! Зачем вы {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} слушаете?»

uk.L: А багато з них казали: «Він має біса і несамовитий; чого ви {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} слухаєте?»
uk.B: Багато з них казали: «У {{deity_pronoun:ньому|Ньому}} біс, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не при собі. Навіщо {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} слухати?»
uk.R: Багато з них казали: «Біс довів {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} до божевілля! Чому ви {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} слухаєте?»

ja.L: 彼らのうちの多くの者が言っていた。「あの男は悪霊を持っていて、狂っている。なぜあの男[の言うこと]を聞くのか？」
ja.B: 彼らのうちの多くの者は言った。「あの男は悪霊に取りつかれて、正気を失っている。なぜ、あんな男の言うことを聞くのか？」
ja.R: その多くの人が言いました。「あの男は、悪霊のせいで頭がおかしくなっているのだ！なぜ、あんな男の言うことを聞くのか？」

decisions.choice: he has a demon and is raving: he is mad, in the grip of an evil spirit
alternatives: two separate charges, possession and madness
decisions.reason: Here the two charges stand side by side, and the second explains the first: to say someone "has a demon" was a way of calling him mad (7:20; 8:48, 52). The verb (μαίνομαι) means to rave, to be out of one's mind (Acts 12:15; 26:24-25). It is an insult rather than a diagnosis.

decisions.choice: were saying: the imperfect shows talk that went on among them
decisions.reason: The tense describes what many were saying, and others were saying in reply (verse 21). It pictures the argument among the hearers.

decisions.choice: why do you listen to him?: a question meant to stop others listening
alternatives: a real question asking for a reason
decisions.reason: The question is aimed at those who are still listening: there is no reason to give attention to a madman. The irony is that the sheep do listen to the shepherd's voice (verses 3, 16, 27).

decisions.choice: out of his mind (B); A demon has driven him mad (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both charges and gives the second in an everyday phrase. Readable joins them into one, as 8:48 does, showing that the demon is the cause of the madness (meaning decision m1). It keeps the demon, because verse 21 answers that very word.

decisions.choice: ha perdido el juicio (B); un demonio lo ha vuelto loco (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the second charge explains the first (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "ông ta" with no deity_pronoun span in the mouths of those who reject him
alternatives: "Ngài" with the span, as the English keeps its span
decisions.reason: Style guide section 6: opponents speak of Jesus as "ông ta"; a reverent "Ngài" in their mouths would be false to the scene, so the setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: "các anh" for the hearers addressing one another
decisions.reason: Ordinary people among themselves use "các anh" (style guide section 6).

decisions.choice: The hostile hearers speak of Jesus without honorifics ("그는", "그 사람"), in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: The speakers are calling him mad; giving them honorific forms would put respect in their mouths that the scene does not have (style guide, section 4). The narrator keeps the honorific for Jesus.

decisions.choice: plain "उसमें", "उसकी" for Jesus in the crowd's mouth
decisions.reason: The crowd and his opponents speak of Jesus plainly among themselves, as settled in Matthew; the narrator keeps the honorific.

decisions.choice: "悪霊を持っていて、狂っている" (L); "悪霊に取りつかれて、正気を失っている" (B); "悪霊のせいで頭がおかしくなっている" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek's two charges as written; Balanced uses the Japanese idiom for possession; Readable joins them, the demon causing the madness (m1), and keeps the demon because verse 21 answers that word. The hostile hearers speak of Jesus as "あの男".

source.text: ἄλλοι ἔλεγον· Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα οὐκ ἔστιν δαιμονιζομένου· μὴ δαιμόνιον δύναται τυφλῶν ὀφθαλμοὺς ἀνοῖξαι;

records.literal_gloss: Others were saying, "These the sayings not are of one demon-possessed; not a demon is able of blind [ones] eyes to open?"

en.L: Others were saying, "These are not the sayings of one who has a demon. A demon is not able to open [the] eyes of [the] blind, is it?"
en.B: Others said, "This is not how a man with a demon speaks. Surely a demon cannot open the eyes of the blind?"
en.R: Others said, "Someone who has a demon does not talk like this. And can a demon make blind people able to see? Of course not!"

es.L: Otros decían: «Estas palabras no son de un endemoniado. ¿Acaso puede un demonio abrir los ojos de los ciegos?».
es.B: Otros decían: «Así no habla alguien que tiene un demonio. ¿Puede acaso un demonio abrir los ojos a los ciegos?».
es.R: Otros decían: «Alguien que tiene un demonio no habla así. ¿Y puede un demonio hacer que los ciegos vean? ¡Claro que no!».

fr.L: D’autres disaient : « Ces paroles ne sont pas celles d’un possédé. Un démon peut-il ouvrir [les] yeux [des] aveugles ? »
fr.B: D’autres disaient : « Ce n’est pas ainsi que parle un homme possédé par un démon. Un démon pourrait-il ouvrir les yeux des aveugles ? »
fr.R: D’autres disaient : « Quelqu’un qui a un démon ne parle pas comme ça. Et est-ce qu’un démon peut rendre la vue aux aveugles ? Bien sûr que non ! »

sw.L: Wengine walikuwa wakisema, "Haya si maneno ya mtu mwenye pepo. Je, pepo anaweza kufumbua macho ya vipofu?"
sw.B: Wengine walisema, "Hivi sivyo anavyosema mtu mwenye pepo. Hakika pepo hawezi kufumbua macho ya vipofu?"
sw.R: Wengine walisema, "Mtu mwenye pepo hasemi hivi. Tena, je, pepo anaweza kuwawezesha vipofu kuona? Hapana!"

vi.L: Những người khác nói: "Những lời này không phải của người bị quỷ ám. Lẽ nào quỷ có thể mở mắt người mù sao?"
vi.B: Những người khác nói: "Người bị quỷ ám đâu có nói như thế. Quỷ làm sao mở mắt cho người mù được?"
vi.R: Người khác lại nói: "Người bị quỷ ám không nói như thế này. Mà quỷ có thể làm cho người mù nhìn thấy được sao? Chắc chắn là không!"

ko.L: 다른 사람들은 말하고 있었다. "이것은 귀신 들린 사람의 말들이 아니다. 귀신이 눈먼 사람들의 눈을 뜨게 할 수 있겠느냐?"
ko.B: 다른 사람들은 말했다. "귀신 들린 사람은 이렇게 말하지 않는다. 귀신이 어떻게 눈먼 사람의 눈을 뜨게 할 수 있겠느냐?"
ko.R: 그러나 다른 사람들은 말했다. "귀신 들린 사람은 이런 말을 하지 않는다. 귀신이 눈먼 사람을 보게 할 수 있겠느냐? 절대 그럴 수 없다!"

pt.L: Outros diziam: "Essas não são palavras de um endemoninhado. Acaso um demônio pode abrir [os] olhos de cegos?"
pt.B: Outros diziam: "Não é assim que fala um homem que tem demônio. Por acaso um demônio pode abrir os olhos dos cegos?"
pt.R: Outros diziam: "Quem tem um demônio não fala desse jeito. E será que um demônio pode fazer cegos enxergarem? É claro que não!"

am.L: ሌሎች እንዲህ ይሉ ነበር፦ «እነዚህ ቃላት ጋኔን ያደረበት ሰው ቃላት አይደሉም። ጋኔን የዕውሮችን ዓይኖች መክፈት ይችላል እንዴ?»
am.B: ሌሎች ግን እንዲህ አሉ፦ «ጋኔን ያደረበት ሰው እንዲህ አይናገርም። ጋኔን የዕውሮችን ዓይኖች ሊከፍት ይችላል እንዴ?»
am.R: ሌሎች ግን እንዲህ አሉ፦ «ጋኔን ያደረበት ሰው እንዲህ አይናገርም። ደግሞስ ጋኔን ዓይነ ስውሮች እንዲያዩ ማድረግ ይችላል? በፍጹም!»

hi.L: दूसरे कहने लगे, "ये बातें दुष्टात्मा से ग्रस्त [मनुष्य] की नहीं हैं। क्या दुष्टात्मा अंधों की आँखें खोल सकती है?"
hi.B: दूसरों ने कहा, "दुष्टात्मा से ग्रस्त आदमी ऐसी बातें नहीं करता। भला दुष्टात्मा अंधों की आँखें कैसे खोल सकती है?"
hi.R: दूसरों ने कहा, "जिसमें दुष्टात्मा हो, वह ऐसी बातें नहीं करता। और क्या कोई दुष्टात्मा अंधों को देखने लायक़ बना सकती है? बिलकुल नहीं!"

ru.L: Другие говорили: «Это не слова одержимого бесом. Разве бес может открыть глаза слепым?»
ru.B: Другие говорили: «Так не говорит человек, в котором бес. Неужели бес может открыть глаза слепым?»
ru.R: А другие говорили: «Человек, в котором бес, так не говорит. И разве бес может сделать так, чтобы слепые видели? Конечно, нет!»

uk.L: Інші казали: «Це не слова того, хто має біса. Хіба біс може відкрити очі сліпим?»
uk.B: Інші казали: «Людина, в якій біс, так не говорить. Хіба біс може відкрити очі сліпим?»
uk.R: Інші казали: «Хто має біса, той так не говорить. І хіба біс може зробити сліпих зрячими? Звісно, ні!»

ja.L: ほかの者たちは言っていた。「これらは、悪霊に取りつかれた者の言葉ではない。まさか、悪霊が目の見えない者たちの目を開けることができるだろうか？」
ja.B: ほかの者たちは言った。「これは、悪霊に取りつかれた人の話し方ではない。悪霊が、目の見えない人の目を開けられるはずがないではないか？」
ja.R: ほかの人たちは言いました。「悪霊に取りつかれた人は、こんな話し方はしない。それに、悪霊が目の見えない人を見えるようにできるだろうか？できるはずがない！」

decisions.choice: these sayings: what he says shows a sound mind, not a demon's raving
decisions.reason: They answer the charge of verse 20. The word (ῥῆμα) means things said; they find his words clear and full of sense, not the talk of a man possessed.

decisions.choice: can a demon open ...?: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question begins with a word (μή) that expects "no". They do not merely deny the charge; they argue from the sign: giving sight is a work of God, not of a demon.

decisions.choice: open the eyes of the blind: the healing of the man born blind (chapter 9)
decisions.reason: The speakers point back to the sign of 9:1-7, and use the man's own argument (9:30-33): no one had ever opened the eyes of someone born blind, and only one from God could do it. The Scriptures speak of opening the eyes of the blind as God's work (Psalm 146:8; Isaiah 35:5; 42:7). As in 9:16, some draw the right conclusion from the sign.

decisions.choice: This is not how a man with a demon speaks (B); Someone who has a demon does not talk like this (R)
alternatives: These are not the sayings of one who has a demon (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the point in a natural English sentence. The speakers mean Jesus, a particular man, so Balanced says "a man".

decisions.choice: Surely ... cannot (B); Of course not! (R)
alternatives: A demon is not able ..., is it? (Literal)
decisions.reason: Each level shows that the question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso ...? (L, B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: Each level shows that the question expects "no" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Un démon pourrait-il ... ? (B); Bien sûr que non ! (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no (meaning decision m2). French shows this at Balanced with the conditional ("pourrait-il"), which voices doubt; Readable adds the answer, as the English Readable does. Literal keeps the plain question.

decisions.choice: "Lẽ nào ... sao?" (L); "làm sao ... được?" (B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks a question that expects "no" with "lẽ nào" or "làm sao ... được", which does the work of Greek me.

decisions.choice: "... 할 수 있겠느냐?" (L); "어떻게 ... 할 수 있겠느냐?" (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects the answer no; the Korean rhetorical ending -겠느냐 carries that expectation without a tag.

decisions.choice: "ዕውሮች" (the blind, L, B); "ዓይነ ስውሮች" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 9: "ዕውር" is the plain written word, and Readable uses the gentler everyday "ዓይነ ስውር".

decisions.choice: "まさか……できるだろうか" (L); "……はずがないではないか" (B); "できるはずがない！" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level shows that the question expects the answer no (m2).
